claims: You can get sued before making your first dollar with a vibe-coded app
1. Paperwork: terms of service, privacy policy, cookie notice; creator did these before writing a line of Ducktate code; missing docs 'can cost up to $25 per violation' (as stated)
2. Consent: if using PostHog analytics/session replay, keep session replay off until consent is obtained (likely off by default); violations 'up to $5K per violation'
3. Database: row-level security, understand authorization vs authentication; a data leak can shut down the business
Creator has 6 years building enterprise software; full learning module and prompts on ducktate.com under Learn
how_to_steps: Draft ToS, privacy policy, and cookie notice before launch (use an open-source legal template repo)
Configure analytics (PostHog) so session replay only runs after user consent
Enable row-level security on the database (Supabase) and separate authentication from authorization logic
Use the prompt cheat sheet at ducktate.com/learn before the production push

relevance.why: Solid pre-launch checklist for a solo founder shipping apps fast: legal docs, consent-gated analytics, RLS. Fines quoted are vague, but the three items are real exposure areas for every app we ship.
